questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience life in Australia and study at a university with a strong reputation in psychology, which made the University of Melbourne the ideal choice

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy – there were many resources and support services available for students to find information and get help when needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 on campus was very helpful and provided clear answers to any questions I had upon arrival

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to find affordable housing. I first looked into student accommodation through the university, but most options were very expensive. I eventually found a room through Flexi Stayz — the process was easy, but it was also expensive. I shared a room with a friend in a house with 11 people and only two toilets, and the living conditions weren’t great. I know others had better luck finding cheaper rooms through the Facebook group “Fairy Floss.”

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult to find a good place at a reasonable price. I recommend starting the search several months in advance and connecting with other exchange students to look for housing together.

questions.answer: The registration process was described step by step on the University's website

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful — I was lucky to get all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the instructions from the website. If you need help, go to Stop 1 or ask other exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level was quite similar to what I experienced at the University of Copenhagen. At the University of Melbourne, the final grade is based on a combination of a mid-semester exam, assignments, and an end-of-semester exam, which spread the workload throughout the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style included lectures and mandatory tutorials, similar to the structure at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- PSYC30014 The Psychopathology of Everyday Life
- PSYC20008 Developmental Psychology
- MECM30013 Marketing Communications
- EDUC20064 Concepts of childhood

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course Psychopathology of Everyday Life. It was really interesting. Additionally, I was able to get it pre-approved as equivalent to “Klinisk 2” at my home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many activities available - everything you can imagine. I joined the surf club’s camp, which was really fun and a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfclub

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are so many things to see and do. I recommend exploring the Great Ocean Road, the Grampians, and Mount Martha. Within Melbourne, areas like Fitzroy and Brunswick are also great for food, culture, and local vibes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don’t hesitate to talk to other students early on, especially during tutorials. Joining social clubs is also a great way to meet local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find the cultural differences themselves challenging. However, it could be a bit difficult to make close local friends, as many already have established social circles, jobs, and routines.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how open, friendly, and outgoing Australian people are. It made everyday interactions feel welcoming and relaxed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start looking for housing several months before your exchange, as it can be difficult to find something affordable.

2. Begin applying for scholarships (legater) and keep track of deadlines as soon as you’ve been accepted for exchange.

3. Don’t hesitate to reach out to other UCPH students going on exchange - it can be really helpful to connect before you arrive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for as many scholarships as possible — you might be lucky and receive financial support that can really help during your exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great people that I've met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The biggest challenges were keeping up with the academic workload and finding suitable housing, especially at a reasonable price.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
